01

Install. Check. You’re ready to plan.

Prepare Node.js 24.x, pnpm 11.25.0 and Git. Clone this engine into a short local Windows path, then run its setup check.

Need the prerequisites? +

Use the official downloads below. Select Node.js 24.x and the Windows x64 installers. After installing Node and Git, reopen your terminal and install the pinned pnpm version.

Node.js downloads — choose 24.x ↗ · Git for Windows ↗

AFTER NODE IS INSTALLED
npm install --global pnpm@11.25.0
TERMINAL
git clone https://github.com/lyhys12345/github-video-engine.git
cd github-video-engine
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
pnpm gve doctor --first-owner
Install what you need for the next step.
Your next stepWhat you need
Plan & reviewGit, Node 24.x, pnpm 11.25.0 and writable local storage. Use your existing Codex account; no separate model API key.
Render videoAdd Chrome/Chromium, FFmpeg and FFprobe.
Add narrationImport authorized WAVs, or set up a supported local voice. Only the local neural voice route needs the separate NVIDIA/Python setup.
WHAT TO LOOK FOR

Look for planning.status: ready. That means the local runtime and storage checks passed. Media checks marked not-checked can wait until after script review.

Read the setup check +
ready
The listed checks passed for this phase.
blocked
Resolve the reported blocker, then run the check again.
not-checked
Outside this check’s scope. This is expected for media during planning.
awaiting-selection
Preview setup still needs an explicit voice and language choice.

Doctor checks locally; it does not contact GitHub, launch a browser or generate media. Source capture checks access to your public repository later.

Setup details & troubleshooting ↗
02

Open the engine folder in Codex.

Use the github-video-engine folder you just cloned as your working project. Its github-explainer skill is included. Your target repository is an input link, not a project you need to install or run.

Use your existing Codex session.

The repository includes the github-explainer skill and project instructions. Open the engine folder and ask in ordinary language. No separate API key or global skill copy is needed for this route.

Codex walkthrough ↗

The session route does not need a separate model API key. Your coding-agent account and usage terms still apply. Claude Code is an alternative entry with a narrower verification status; see Compatibility below.

03

Give it a link and an audience.

Copy the example below, or tailor it here. The agent can suggest the creative direction; you do not need to design every scene yourself.

Browser-only. Nothing is submitted, stored or generated on a server.

Example prompt below. Replace OWNER/REPO before using it, or enter your repository above.

COPY INTO YOUR CODEX CHAT
Use github-explainer to explain https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.
Audience: people who have never used this project.
Plan a concise vertical short video. Choose the duration and style to suit the story.
Start with one useful result, then explain what makes it possible.
For this step, research and prepare the full narration, shot-by-shot storyboard and source evidence only.
Obtain an independent script review and fix supported findings. Show me the revised script for approval.
Do not generate media or execute the target repository. Before any later rendering, clarify the supported visual assets and voice route with me.

This prompt asks for script review only. Voice and media generation come after your approval and a compatible setup.

04

Approve the story. Then make it move.

The agent researches the repository and prepares the full narration, storyboard and sources. Independent script review helps catch issues before you see the revised draft. Read it, ask for changes, and approve the actual version you want produced.

Your first successful stop is awaiting-script-review: the draft is ready for you. If you see awaiting-session-agent first, let Codex continue reading the source packet and authoring the script.

“Show the result first. Then explain the one idea that makes it work.”
THE NEXT CHECKPOINT

Before rendering, choose a supported visual and voice route with the agent. Rendering needs Chrome/Chromium, FFmpeg and FFprobe; local synthesis has additional requirements below. A changed script needs renewed approval.

Source capture is not a finished video. Review the resulting picture and sound yourself; technical checks and agent reviews do not replace your final acceptance.

05

Keep the result. And the project.

Supported exports include an MP4 and editable story, animation, caption definitions and source records. You can return to that project to revise it, instead of starting again.

“Shorten the opening and use a clearer example.”

Reopen the engine project and ask your agent. It revises the plan for your approval, then reuses valid unchanged work when making the next version.

story.jsonnarrative.jsonanimation.jsonrun.json
What the export includes +

This is an editable engine project, not a Premiere or CapCut project. Supported narrated packages can preserve selected original WAVs. Packages exclude credentials, local voice profiles, model weights and environments. Transfer the entire package plus its digest, and install a compatible engine to continue on another machine.

Export & import guide ↗

WHEN YOU ARE READY TO RENDER

A voice route that fits your setup.

The voices heard in some demos are private configurations, not bundled presets. Choose from these supported routes with the agent.

Free public local voices +

Ryan for English and Serena for Chinese. No reference recording or paid TTS account is required. Separate setup: Windows x64, Python 3.12.14 and NVIDIA CUDA with native BF16 support. RTX 3070 has been exercised. The model download is about 2.50 GB, plus runtime and CUDA space.

Install the public voice runtime ↗
Bring your own audio or local voice +

Import authorized finished WAV recordings that match the approved scene text, or configure an authorized supported local voice. Anna/Chen reference recordings and private profiles are not distributed. A missing voice produces an explicit error rather than silently changing your choice.

Voice preference details ↗
Start with a silent technical preview +

Explicitly choose silence to review supported diagrams and visual transformations without a voice model. Some storyboard titles, copy and transitions can remain export-only. Real product footage and editorial cuts need the separate showcase route and authorized assets; silent technical support does not promise every planned scene can render.

Supported media routes ↗

COMPATIBILITY

Know your starting point.

Recommended: Windows + Codex +

Windows x64/NTFS, Node 24, SQLite and same-volume hard links are the verified environment. Real Codex URL-to-narrated-media and feedback continuation are documented with operator involvement. Native macOS/Linux execution is unverified, and automatic reproduction of the showcase is not guaranteed.

Claude Code and BYO API status +

Claude Code project routing is statically checked; real end-to-end media generation and revision remain unverified. Optional BYO API authoring is experimental, with real-provider interoperability unverified. The Codex session route needs no separate model API key; the host still has its own account and usage requirements.
